angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,490,885 km at 89.77 pc = 0.22 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: distance 89.767 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.019), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 89.767 +/- 1.706 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 11.0065 +/- 0.0162 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96), 677.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.143 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: radius 2.143 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 4.032 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,490,885 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5591 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: effective temperature 5591 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: effective temperature 5591 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 48265 (pscomppars): spectral type G5 IV/V, from Wu et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..189W/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 48265: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 48265 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.39 dex, from Wu et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..189W/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 48265 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.58433, from Jenkins et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017MNRAS.466..443J/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 48265 (pscomppars): age 4.201 Gyr, from Barbato et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...615A.175B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 48265 (pscomppars): rotation period 45 d, from Barbato et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...615A.175B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 48265 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3.1 km/s, from Jenkins et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017MNRAS.466..443J/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.02 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 8 published values span log g 3.92 to 4.09, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
